subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single runnable TypeScript module that builds a qilin using the 3D builder SDK, keeping the implementation focused but high-quality while being careful to only use valid API calls from the library.

I'm sketching out the design: a quadruped horse-like body with scales, a dragon-like head, antlers, cloud-style mane and tail, and hooves, sized roughly 2.2m tall and 2.4m long facing forward. Now I'm starting to define the skeleton joints for the creature.

Still defining joints and chains...

I'll define each leg as a four-point polyline (hip, knee, ankle, toe) giving four named joints per limb, placing front legs further forward in z and back legs further back, with left side on positive X.

For the leg sweeps, I'm tapering the radius from thick at the hip to thin at the ankle using a simple linear function of the sweep parameter. Then I'm adding hoof caps as small cylinders attached explicitly to the tip joint of each leg, colored dark or gold.

Now I'm shaping the torso as a sweep along a curved path from the hip/tail area to the chest, bound to the hips and spine bones, with a radius profile that bulges larger toward the chest using a sine-based taper, and I'm laying out the catmull points for that body path.

Defining the body radius function to taper toward the shoulder, then planning the coat colors using a cel-shaded toon style for a high-fantasy anime look — golden-amber body with darker scale shading and a cloud-white mane.

Finalizing specific hex colors for the coat, belly, mane, antlers, and hooves, and now considering how to texture the cloud-mane using SVG cloud shapes layered on the neck and back.

For the tail, cards chain backward from the hips. I'm designing the cloud texture as a cluster of white circles with blue-stroked outlines to give that puffy mane look. Now thinking through antlers — branching with fleshy tips, probably built as sweeps along curved paths since the head geometry isn't established yet for sprouting.

Computing antler attachment points relative to the head joint, resolving which local direction words correspond to model-left versus right, and mapping those into bezier paths for the sweep geometry.

Now I'm sketching the skull itself as a scaled sphere geometry positioned at the head bone, adjusting the scale factors to give it a slightly elongated, flattened shape.

Next I'm adding a muzzle swept along a bezier path from the skull to the jaw front, tapering its radius, plus a separate jaw sweep. For the eyes, I'm planning to use decals applied to the skull's surface, positioning them with directional offsets around the skull.

For the body, I'm thinking about giving the qilin a scaled texture using a golden scale pattern with darker edges, wrapped in a cel shader to keep the stylized look consistent with the rest of the paint.

Now I'm adding a glowing jade gem on the forehead, positioning it using a surface hit point and attaching a small octahedron geometry there with a glow effect applied to the resulting part.

For the tail, I'm building a chain of segments sweeping backward from the hips, tapering the radius toward the tip, and scattering card elements along the tail chain's later points to create a cloud-like wisp effect at the end.

Tail puffs should lean along the tangent with backward flow. For the mane, I'll scatter cloud cards along the upper neck surface using a filter on the normal's y-component, with a backward-and-up flow direction. I'll skip the foreleg cuffs and dorsal ribbon for now to keep things simpler.

Next I need to set up the leg chains as polylines with four named joints each (hip, knee, ankle, hoof), giving three spans so the hoof lands as the tip joint. The leg sweep will taper the radius from hip to hoof, blending into the body radius at the top, with the chain automatically driving the sweep geometry.

Front legs parent to an upper spine joint while back legs parent to the hips, and I'm naming left/right sides with L/R suffixes to keep joint names unique. The hoof itself is a small cylinder bone attached to the tip joint, sized and positioned so its base sits right at ground level, painted dark with a possible gold ring accent.

I need to set the foot joint height to match the leg tube's radius so the cylinder cap sits flush at y=0 without sinking through the floor, and make the hoof slightly wider than the leg tube for a visible taper into the hoof shape. For the neck, I'm running a curve from the spine's end point up to the head joint, keeping the overall qilin height around 2.3 units at the antler tips.

Now I'm setting up the imports from the builder library (createBuilder, rng, bezier, catmull, polyline, svg, paint, scales, mottle, toon/cel helpers, glow) and planning the mane material using a cel-shaded cloud texture in a neutral white tone, then sketching an SVG cloud pattern with blue-tinted circles for the texture.

I'm now working out the antler geometry: two sweeping bezier curves per side built from head-local coordinates (left/up/forward offsets), with a main beam and a secondary branch sweep, mirroring left and right using a sign multiplier.

Working out the head joint position and forward direction so the antler coordinates align correctly with the skull.

Now I'm sketching the jaw geometry - placing the jaw joint behind the head joint, then sweeping a bone shape from the jaw hinge forward to the chin tip, plus a separate upper muzzle sweep curving from the head forward.

I'm figuring out bone inheritance for these sweeps: points built from head.local ride the head bone automatically, but for the jaw I need to explicitly pass the jaw bone so it rides correctly. I'm also blocking out the skull as a sphere part attached to the head bone, scaled to be slightly elongated, and starting to set up a surface accessor on the skull for placing the eyes.

Now I'm working through placing eyes via raycast hits on the skull surface, guarding against null hits before placing the decal, then adding a glowing octahedron gem near the forehead using a similar hit-based placement. I'm skipping nostrils and mouth detail to save budget, and starting to sketch out a simple extruded ear shape attached near the side of the head.

Working out ear orientation...

With thickness extruded along X and the outline spanning Z/Y, the ear ends up thin sideways and wide vertically — sticking up but flat, which reads correctly as an ear shape.

Now I'm defining the extrusion parameters for ears, like thickness, color, and bone attachment, keeping the inner ear detail skipped for simplicity. Then I move to the tail sweep and cloud-like tail cards, before sketching the body's spine path using a catmull-rom curve through hip-to-chest points, figuring out how the bone chain should separately track that spine path.

I'm working out a radius function for the body's taper along the spine path, testing a sine-based formula so the chest end comes out slimmer than the hips, landing on one that gives a reasonable shape. For body coloring I'm combining a countershaded coat and belly tone, then applying a cel-shading pass on top.

Still defining colors...

For the mane and tail I'll use cloud-textured cards, and I'm considering whether to add gold accents like leg rings or a collar, but I'll likely skip those extra details and keep it simpler.

Deciding to skip dorsal flame details and hoof rim accents, keeping just dark hooves. I'm checking proportions—leg length, body height, neck scale—then working out the neck's tapering radius to place mane cards along its surface.

Scattering mane card hits along the neck sweep surface, filtering for upward and backward-facing normals, then placing leaning, flowing cards with some bend and variation. I'm cleaning up the variable naming, settling on neckChain and neckSweep instead of the generic neck name, and skipping extra mane along the back. Now moving on to building the tail chain and its sweep geometry.

I'll skip the gold crown accent for simplicity and just finalize the export metadata, then start writing the actual TypeScript code carefully.

Writing qilin builder code...

Building the spine chain...

Setting up the jaw joint position, then sweeping the body mesh along a spine path with hips and spine bones, and now starting a loop to build the legs symmetrically on each side.

Defining leg joint positions for hips, knees, ankles, and feet, adjusting forward/backward offsets so front legs bend differently than back legs for a natural quadruped stance.

Still writing leg geometry...

Building the skull as a scaled sphere mesh attached to the head bone, then sweeping a tapered bezier curve for the muzzle shape with rounded end caps, both using the body color.

Skipping the nose/muzzle detail for now, I'll add horns and set up eyes positioned on the skull surface, choosing a teal iris color for a more fantastical look. I need to guard against the decal placement call returning null when finding points around the eye center.

For the forehead gem I'm attaching a small glowing octahedron to a brow point if one's found. Then for the ears I'm extruding a curved shape with a sharp point on each side, but I'm running into a TypeScript typing issue with mixed tuple arrays for the outline points and need to type them as const to fix inference.

I'm simplifying the ear outline by dropping the "sharp" tag entirely and just using plain coordinate pairs, which avoids the typing headache since smoothing at zero still gives the right shape. Now I'm moving to the tail, building a chain of bones along a curved path starting near the hips joint, and checking the starting position lines up correctly with the hip joint's location.

Now I'm sweeping that tail chain with a tapering radius and coloring it to match the leg color, then setting up a cloud SVG texture for tufts. I'm also building the neck surface by sweeping the neck chain with a tapered profile, then scattering mane hits across its surface using a filter on the normal's y-component to control where the mane strands appear, and finally draping cloud cards over the neck top tinted white to look like a fluffy mane.

Still adding cloud scatter details — more cards on the back spine with a similar normal filter, plus tail tuft cards generated along the tail chain using backward-facing frames. I'm deciding to skip extra embellishments like gold hoof bands or a chest pendant to keep things simple, and wrapping up by returning the root object while double-checking option names like iris color and imports for countershade, scales, and bezier/catmull curve helpers.

I'm confirming the remaining imports needed, including polyline, rng, svg, and createBuilder from root, glow from the glow kit, and cel/animeEye from the toon kit, plus standard Three.js geometry classes. Now I'm setting up small typed helper functions, like one that converts forward/up/left values into local head coordinates, so the final antler and head-building code stays concise and properly typed before writing it all out.
